speaker: gm
text: The yard smells of wet grain, pigeons and river mud. A small grey-coated clerk turns slowly from the sack hoist above the shut loft door, a pigeon perched on the beam beside him. Below, a scrawny boy in boots much too large for him pelts the body with gutter stones. “Hold still, you miserable coat-hanger!” From the wall, a sharp-faced girl in a shawl swears at him in Common, then Saltmere dock cant. Sergeant Kell steps away from the gate, notebook open. “Agnes Kell, investigator. The Captain calls it suicide. I’m here to see what can be sworn to.” A stone clangs off the hoist hook. The clerk turns a little faster. What do you do?

speech.tag: the boy in the too-big boots
speech.speaker: cob

marks.note: Kell writes down what happened, and in the granary quarter people take “Kell’s written it down” to mean it’s true—and too late.

speaker: player
text: (I take a close look at Wendell Prout's body)

speaker: dice
text: Medicine check to tell how Prout really died: 16 + 1 = 17 vs DC 12: success

speaker: gm
text:
Up close, the slanting burn of the hoist rope crosses a thinner, level cord mark low on Prout’s neck. There is a swelling beneath the hair at the back of his skull, and his palms are clean: no rope burn. The hanging did not kill him. He was struck, strangled, and hoisted afterward.

Kell writes, then reads back the entry. “A second cord mark. Blunt swelling to the back of the head. Clean palms. Cause of death inconsistent with hanging.” Her gaze shifts to the stones in the boy’s hands. “Noted.”

The girl on the wall stops drumming her heels. The boy’s next stone stays in his fist.

speaker: player
text: You two... did you see what happened?

speaker: dice
text: Persuasion check to find out whether you two saw what happened: 12 + 2 = 14 vs DC 15: failure

speaker: gm
text:
The boy’s eyes flick to Kell’s notebook. He edges toward the water butt, stones clenched tight. “Cob don’t talk to bluebottles.” He spits into the mud.

“Shut it, Cob.” She keeps her gaze on the open gate.

Kell makes a brief entry. “Witnesses questioned. No account given.” Neither child offers anything about what happened in the night.

speech.tag: the boy in the too-big boots
speech.speaker: cob

marks.note: You came with Kell, and Cob sees her as a bluebottle—a watch officer. He won’t talk to the watch.
Cob spits after refusing to talk to the watch. You asked him questions with Kell standing there.

speaker: player
text: Perhaps a shilling would change your mind?

speaker: gm
text:
Cob looks at the shilling, then at you. He pockets it with a swift little nod, as if a proper business has been concluded. “One shilling? For a look at Cob’s boot? You must think Cob’s a charity.” He stamps the left one. It gives a dry crackle. “There. You heard it. That’s what you get.”

He backs another step towards the water butt, boots still firmly on his feet. “They’re Mister Prout’s, all right. Cob found ’em. Nobody’s having them. Not the watch, not my da, not some bleedin’ pawnshop.”

The girl on the wall watches the gate. Kell makes a note. “One shilling offered for access to the boy’s boot. Access refused. Noted.”

speaker: player
text: (I clench my fists in a barely controlled rage) You'll give that shilling back or tell me what you know if you know what's good for you (the red mist rises. This is no idle threat)

speaker: dice
text: Intimidation check to force the children to reveal what they know: 11 + 4 = 15 vs DC 12: success

speaker: gm
text:
Cob’s stones slip from his fist. His eyes shine, and he stares hard at the cobbles as the words come out.

“There were two men. Mister Prout was arguing with ’em in the loft. Silvertop—the posh cove with the silver cane. And a big one with his hand all bandaged. Big one said, ‘Yes, Master.’ Then there was a thump, and Mister Prout made a choking noise. The hoist creaked after. There weren’t any sacks on it.”

The girl in the shawl flings her silver crown into the mud. “You great red-eyed bastard. You’ve just told them where Cob was.”

Kell writes without looking up. “Witness: boy, name withheld. Two men heard in the loft. One addressed as Master. Noted.”

speaker: gm
text:
Cob stares at you, still pale. The girl in the shawl shifts on the wall, putting herself between him and the yard gate.

“Silvertop. That’s what Cob called him. Silver cane, posh coat. You heard the rest.”

“You’ve scared him half out of his boots, and now you want him to say it twice?”

Kell’s pencil rests against the page. “The witness named him Silvertop. No other name given.”

speaker: player
text: So who's this silvertop? He go by any other names?

speaker: gm
text:
Kell glances up from her notebook. At the word “Silvertop,” her pencil stops for a beat. “I know the name J. Sallow from the Royal Purveyor’s delivery notices. I’ve never met him. I can’t tell you whether he uses another name.”

Cob shifts his weight in the oversized boots. “Silvertop’s what Cob calls him. Silver cane, flower stink. Cob don’t know his proper name.”

The girl in the shawl watches you from the wall, lips pressed tight. Kell resumes writing. “That is what the witness knows. Noted.”

marks.note: The Royal Purveyor’s office supplies the palace, including its grain. Kell knows J. Sallow’s name from its delivery notices.
